Define tests measurable with respect to the buffered score array σ{(Zᵢ¹,Zᵢ²): i∈Iₙ}, and define the usual α/β minimax separation radius. The existing theorem gives the O(n⁻¹ᐟ²) upper bound. For the matching lower bound, use the deterministic line, p=1/2, Eᵢ(d)=dᵢ, and iid Uᵢ∼Unif[0,1]. For s∈[0,1/2], partition Uᵢ into types 0,+,− with probabilities 1−s,s/2,s/2. With any fixed a>0 satisfying a/2≤B, set Yᵢ(d)=a/2 for type 0, Yᵢ(d)=a(2dᵢ−1)/2 for type +, and its negative for type −. Then the score pair is independent Rademacher ±a under type 0 and is identically (+a,+a) or (−a,−a) under types + or −. Hence τ_P=0, hᵢ∈{0,±a} iid, and Ω_pop=a²s. The one-site score-pair probabilities are (1+s)/4 on ++ and -- and (1−s)/4 on +- and -+, so

    KL(Q_s,Q_0)
    = ½[(1+s)log(1+s)+(1−s)log(1−s)]
    ≤ s².

Thus KL(Q_s^N,Q_0^N)≤Ns²; Pinsker and Le Cam imply that no score-measurable level-α test has uniform power 1−β at Ω_pop below c·a²/√N when α+β<1.
